Weekly Markets Monitor - Waller the Dollar

PDF
2.25 mb

Highlights Last week was dominated by leadership turmoil at Nvidia and the resulting volatility in global AI stocks. On the macro front, in the US, elevated CPI and PPI prints, alongside hawkish Fed comments, raised expectations of a December rate hike. Labour markets remained resilient, but housing weakened. Growth strengthened in both the Eurozone and UK, while China saw mixed inflation signals and stronger exports as Beijing extended its trade truce with the US. In India, inflation rose and the trade deficit widened.  Major global equity markets ended the week higher, while bond yields and the US dollar rose and oil prices eased.  The US dollar rose sharply last week, supported by hawkish Fed commentary, including Governor Waller raising the prospect of a 50bp hike in December, stronger-than-expected CPI (0.4% m/m vs 0.3% expected), and resilient US growth and equities (rotation rather than outflows). As a result, the Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index (BBDXY) broke what we view as a cluster of key technical resistance at 1,229/1,233 (C.O.T.W). A sustained hold above here would suggest a large USD base has formed, turning the core trend higher. Alongside rising yields (10-year TIPS yields are up ~30bp in November), this presents a possible “double whammy” headwind for gold for the foreseeable future.
